overrides: week: winner set to a game per the owner; former winner a game is runner-up
year runner_up: replaced a game (repeat of the Month winner) with a game
eligibility: rated standard-chess win in 2026 (both sites, no Chess.com coach/bot games, no variants)
excluded: opponent berserked (Lichess WhiteBerserk/BlackBerserk header, or opponent started with under 60% of the base clock); this removes the +560 the opponent game (the opponent berserked)
excluded: abandonments; wins on time before move 20; any game under 20 moves; Lichess opponents on the provisional 1500 default

excluded: any game where he made a blunder: an engine "Blunder" judgment, or any of his moves where the eval swung 2.00+ pawns against him (mate capped at ±10). Comeback-from-a-blunder wins therefore do not qualify
requires per-move engine data, so blunder-free play can be verified (Chess.com Aug 2–Oct 1 2026 via local Stockfish; Lichess server-analysed games)
data_note: no Lichess games after Sep 23, so the week and month windows contain Chess.com games only

winner.caption: Against a 1688, he struck with 14...Qxd2+!!, flagged Brilliant by Chess.com's Game Review: he hands over the queen because 15.Kxd2 Bxb1 wins White's queen right back, leaving him a full rook up. He ground out the endgame and won on time with 7.6s left.

runner_up.caption: Opponent dropped the h8 rook to 3.Bxg7 and 4.Bxh8, and he never let go: 31 moves of 1-minute bullet at 96.7 accuracy, zero mistakes, until a 1683 resigned.
runner_up.reason: Beat a 1683 (he was 1676) by resignation after 31.Qd6 with 96.7 accuracy / 16.6 ACPL and no blunders (Chess.com 60)
runner_up.why: Honest note: the game was decided on move 3 by the opponent's error, so it earns 0/10 for contest. It still wins because none of the other two eligible games this week comes close on quality: 96.7 accuracy and 16.6 ACPL, against 86.3/51.4 with 3 mistakes for the runner-up and 90.5/29.0 for #3 (who also won on time at move 22). It also ended by resignation, not on the clock.
runner_up.key_move_note: from here his eval stayed at +3.00 or better to the end
runner_up.standout_why: engine's top move; punished the opponent's previous move, eval +0.15→+6.38

week.label: Game of the Week
week.window_note: The 7 days ending Oct 3 (Sep 27–Oct 3) had only 1 eligible game (a game, score 44.4), so the most recent 7-day window with at least 3 eligible games was used. Chess.com data ends Oct 1.

winner.caption: Seventy-one moves of 1-minute bullet as Black against a 1665, with no blunders and only one mistake: level until move 37, then he out-ground the rook endgame, promoted on h1 and mated with 71...Ra5# with about 3 seconds left.
winner.reason: Beat a 1665 (he was 1653) by mate (71...Ra5#) with 94.3 accuracy / 16.9 ACPL and no blunders (Chess.com 60)
winner.why: It is the only top-5 game in September that stayed level into the late middlegame (decided at move 40), so it takes the full 10/10 contest points, plus mate and full length. The runner-up (65.9) and #3 173940096170 (65.4) were cleaner (6 and 5 clean points vs 1), but both were decided earlier, at moves 24 and 27. #4 180007567344 (63.6) had 94.6 accuracy but was won by move 10.
winner.key_move_note: from here his eval stayed at +3.00 or better to the end
winner.standout_why: engine's top move; punished the opponent's previous move, eval +6.77→+10.00

runner_up.caption: 95.1 accuracy as Black in a Closed Sicilian against a 1574: he took the a-file, punished 24.Rb1 with 24...Rxa2 and kept piling on until resignation at move 38.
runner_up.reason: Beat a 1574 (he was 1561) by resignation after 38...Ra1+ with 95.1 accuracy / 20.8 ACPL and no blunders (Chess.com 60)
runner_up.why: Highest accuracy of the September top 3 (95.1, ACPL 20.8, 0 mistakes) and the cleanest of them. It finishes second because it ended by resignation rather than mate and was decided at move 24 rather than move 40. It edges #3 (173940096170, 65.4), whose 31-move length scored fewer length points.
runner_up.key_move_note: from here his eval stayed at +3.00 or better to the end
runner_up.standout_why: engine's top move; punished the opponent's previous move, eval -0.51→+5.03

month.label: Game of the Month
month.window_note: Calendar September used: 45 eligible games vs 25 in the last 30 days (Sep 4–Oct 3). Both windows have the same top 5, and September is the cleaner label.

winner.caption: His best-played game of 2026: as Black in 10-minute rapid against a 2131, 98.5 accuracy, ACPL 10.3 and not even an inaccuracy. He took over after 12...Nd5, won the d-file and queened a pawn before his opponent resigned on move 49.
winner.reason: Beat a 2131 (he was 2068) by resignation after 49...Qxh4 with 98.5 accuracy / 10.3 ACPL and no blunders (Lichess 600+0)
winner.why: It is the only eligible 2026 win over a 2100+ opponent (the next highest is 1990). It has the year's highest accuracy (98.5), full ACPL points (10.3) and a perfect 8/8 clean score, and its opponent-strength score of 12.2 is second only to 12.7. The runner-up (67.2) has the edge on contest and mate, but it beat a 1665 and scored only 1 clean point. The next candidates, 172492846674 (66.1) and 174243299132 (65.9), are bullet wins over opponents rated 1469 and 1574.
winner.key_move_note: from here his eval stayed at +3.00 or better to the end
winner.standout_why: punished the opponent's previous move, eval +0.47→+2.78

runner_up.caption: 52 moves of 1-minute bullet as White against a 1461, blunder-free on the engine pass (93.0 accuracy), and he promotes with checkmate: 52.h8=Q# with 9.0s on his clock.
